findings.evidence: Every storyboard frame and the 25/50/75% stills show the same crowd from the same high angle with no lifted ground and nobody in the air. The caption itself says 'It never shows'.
findings.suggestion: Frame the stomp point from about 8-12 m away at a low angle. Make sure the STOMP[:at] position is inside the shot and Lumi is visible before forcing it. Check the :stomp/:stomp_throw events fired during the recording, and only post once a ring and at least one throw are on screen.
findings.what: The film never shows the feature. Lumi is not visible, no stomp, no outgoing ring, no thrown creatures and no landing thumps. The friends just stand or mill about in all 16 frames.

findings.evidence: At 50% the meadow is a wide sand slope. At 75% the same place is green grass with only a thin path, and the sand is back in the last frame. sp_build! snapshots p0/faces of :wordsand when a stomp starts, and wordsand rebuilds its own mesh. Writing the old p0 back (update! with stale coordinates, or the flat reset) would replace the fresh sand with an old shape.
findings.suggestion: Don't overwrite meshes that other plugins own. Displace them in the shader or with a per-layer offset, or have wordsand sample the stomp grid itself. At the very least, re-read the layer whenever its vertex count or the plot object changes.
findings.what: The sand/path ground layer blinks in and out: the large sand area becomes bare grass, then comes back. The terrain re-mesh is corrupting a layer rather than lifting it.
findings.where: storyboard frames 13-15 vs 12 and 16; one-stomp-at-75.jpg vs one-stomp-at-50.jpg; plugins/stomp.jl sp_build!/sp_layer_draw! (SP_LAYERS includes :wordsand)

findings.evidence: The shot is a high three-quarter view across the meadow edge and sea, with large bushes in the foreground blocking the lower left and lower right.
findings.suggestion: Put the camera lower and closer, slightly side-on to the wavefront, so the ground visibly rises and bodies arc against the sky.
findings.what: The camera is far too high and wide for the subject. Even a working ring 2 m tall would read as a tiny ripple, and the creatures that matter fill only a small part of the frame.

fun_why: Nobody would watch this twice: nothing reacts, nothing is thrown, and the one change is a glitch.
real_change: stomp.jl adds a real 2D damped wave equation on a 0.4 m grid under the island. It is pinned at the shoreline so rings reflect, and a stomp is a Gaussian velocity kick. Each frame the terrain, path and wordsand meshes are displaced and re-normalled from the grid, and creatures ride its height. A creature whose ground rises faster than 0.9 m/s is thrown ballistically, and its landing starts a weaker new source, so you get a chain reaction. It triggers each morning at 10:00, on L when you play as Lumi, or with STOMP[:force]. Creature positions, throws and chain sources are simulated, not just drawn. The film shows none of this. The only visible effect is the layer re-mesh (sp_build!/sp_layer_draw!) apparently swapping the wordsand/path meshes with stale or flat copies, which makes the sand blink.
summary: The caption admits the stomp never shows, and that is accurate. The 9.9 s film is a slowly drifting high view of the meadow: there is no Lumi, no jump, no ring, and nobody gets thrown. The only thing that happens is the big sand patch flipping between sand and bare grass. The code behind it is the most ambitious idea in weeks, but this post shows a rendering bug.
surprise_why: What the film shows is a static meadow with a sand layer that flickers. The ground-as-drum-skin chain reaction is a genuine new piece of physics, but it is only in the code, not on screen.
